title: Endohepatology-Based Reclassification of Treatment Indication in High-Risk MASLD
official: Endohepatology-Based Reclassification of Treatment Indication in High-Risk Patients With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Prospective, Multicenter Observational Study
summary: This prospective observational study evaluates whether endohepatology changes treatment indications in adults at high risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Non-invasive testing is followed, when indicated, by a single-session endohepatology assessment including EUS-guided shear-wave elastography, portal pressure gradient measurement and liver biopsy. The primary outcome is treatment reclassification compared with the prospectively documented non-invasive assessment.

interventions.name: Non-invasive MASLD and portal hypertension assessment

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Written informed consent
* Suspected MASLD
* At least one predefined risk criterion

Exclusion Criteria:

* No evidence of MASLD
* HIV infection
* Previous organ transplantation or TIPS
* Current resmetirom therapy
* Decompensated cirrhosis
* Vascular liver disease
* Contraindication to endoscopy, sedation, or liver biopsy
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Inability to provide informed consent
